source_refs.note: Mode of Tetracycline Action:: a main subheading of 23.2.2 Tetracycline, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 211-211.

items: Bacteriostatic Effect: They stop bacteria from growing and multiplying rather than killing them outright.
Gram-Negative/Positive Action: They are effective against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria.
Targeting Ribosomes: Tetracycline enter bacterial cells and it reversibly bind to the 30S ribosomal subunit of its target cell.
Blocking Protein Production: By binding to the 30S ribosome, they prevent aminoacyl-t RNA from binding to the acceptor site, to inhibit translation and protein synthesis.
